author: kesudh
method: Exact shortest-path-tree warm refinement: radix A*, feasible per-sink bounds, neutral and group reroutes, preserved-route and displacement-chain repair, optional circular integer buckets, multiple CPU search workers, strict final-walk polishing, and exact two-parent minimum-cut crossover following PR24. Our GPU kernels are audited prototypes and did not generate these refinements; selected PR26 public warm starts are attributed to its GPU-accelerated engine. Bounded conflict-based search over static multi-sink trees, alternated with neutral group reroutes; opt-in specialized chain pricing avoids full-grid cost setup. 2026-10-04 adoption update: 1 case(s) where a merged entry's route is strictly better than this entry's previous route are carried verbatim from coordinated_refinement (main 2566f5f1); documented as "retained public route" in the cases list, credited via derived_from. 2026-10-04 sole-first update: stress case_01 improved 1,042,314 -> 1,042,310 by a bounded portfolio refinement (cbs-mixed / portfolio / mixed / cbs configs from the carried route; the portfolio config won; route archived from a mid-run snapshot); the route is again our own refinement, parented on the carried coordinated_refinement route.

derived_from.author: jay-tau
derived_from.note: per-case provenance in `cases`; cases byte-identical to a public entry are carried verbatim and excluded from runtime.json

runtime_hardware: Windows, Intel i7-13700HX, 16 cores/24 threads; actual worker count recorded per command; concurrent Hermes and benchmark workloads. Observed wall times, not normalized.
selection: Best independently legal output per case; ties select shortest measured invocation. The per-case commands disclose benchmark-specific selection. Timed multiworker search is nondeterministic.

cases.runtime_basis: carry step (source bytes written + checker verify)

algorithm_references.method: conflict splitting, adapted to static vertex-disjoint multi-sink trees
algorithm_references.citation: Sharon, Stern, Felner and Sturtevant, Conflict-based search for optimal multi-agent pathfinding

hardware: 13th Gen Intel Core i7-13700HX (16 cores / 24 threads), 31.7 GB RAM, Windows 11
runtime_scope: Per case: the measured wall-clock seconds of the run in this entry's pipeline that produced the shipped route file, timed end to end on that case. Own-refined cases: our chained LNS refinement run (4 worker threads); where the original run was not recoverable, the producing invocation was re-executed and byte-verified. Carried cases: the shipped bytes are a credited public entry's file carried verbatim, so the value is the cost of the step that produced our file (write the source bytes + independent checker verification); the upstream entry's generation time is not ours and is not claimed. Up to 6 such runs executed concurrently during sweeping, so wall-clock times are conservative.
